# wgpu-Beef

Beef bindings for [wgpu-native](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu-native) **v29.0.1.1**,
the version Raptor pins, so a backend written against these matches what Raptor's
WebGPU backend was written against.

`src/webgpu.bf` and `src/wgpu.bf` are GENERATED by `generate.py` from the headers in
`dist/include/webgpu`. A wgpu-native bump is: drop the new headers and libraries in,
re-run the generator, rebuild. Do not hand edit the output.

```
python3 generate.py dist/include/webgpu/webgpu.h src/webgpu.bf
python3 generate.py dist/include/webgpu/wgpu.h   src/wgpu.bf
```

## The two headers

`webgpu.h` is the standard W3C C header every implementation provides, including
Dawn's emdawnwebgpu port that a browser build uses.

`wgpu.h` is wgpu-native's own extension header: adapter enumeration, `wgpuDevicePoll`,
the log callback, `WGPUInstanceExtras` backend forcing, SPIR-V ingestion. **None of it
exists in a browser.** A backend that wants to run on both resolves those entry points
dynamically and null guards every call, which is what Raptor's WebGpuApi does with its
`WEBGPU_NATIVE_EXT_FUNCTIONS` split.

## Platforms

Linux links `libwgpu_native.so` directly. Windows needs the import library
`dist/lib/x64/wgpu_native.dll.lib` beside the DLL; Raptor vendors only the DLL because
it loads the sidecar at run time, so that file has to come from the wgpu-native release.
